solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boasted about day being jam-packed

indicators.note: one word goes about another, wrapping round it on both sides

parts.note: to crow is to boast, past tense
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone bragged that the day was packed solid with engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: D sits inside CROWED, between the W and the E, to give CROWDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is full of people is packed tight, the same idea as being stuffed solid.

clue.text: Prison ship getting old American irritable

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
a tanker is a ship carrying oil or other liquid
O is a common abbreviation for old
US stands for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A grumpy old American is held aboard a prison hulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bad-tempered and quarrelsome is easily annoyed, which is a close synonym of this word.

clue.text: Rising stench on fish with note "past sell by date"

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a sole is a flatfish
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A smelly piece of fish comes with a label saying it has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the stench word is read upwards; BO for body odour is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods beyond their expiry are out of date and no longer usable, which is what outdated or superseded things are.

clue.text: Judge river minute

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales/England
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.definitionFit: To consider or regard something in a particular way is to form an opinion of it, as one does when weighing it up.

clue.text: Hold back noise around estimated time of arrival

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
ETA is the usual abbreviation spelled out here

explanation.surface: Delays and racket surround a flight's expected landing time.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone from leaving, such as in custody, is to restrain or keep them in place.

clue.text: Rather inferior doctor about to ingest opiate initially

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of opiate
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A second-rate doctor is about to swallow some opiate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'about to ingest', but it supplies its own letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only average in quality, not very good, is a little below standard.

clue.text: Regularly connected previously

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Two things that used to be linked on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean at some former time, formerly, in the sense of a thing having happened before.

clue.text: Unchanging surface with cross removed

indicators.note: removed tells us a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: the surface is the outside part
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A face that never alters once a cross has been taken off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever, without beginning or end, means never altering over time.

clue.text: Safely grinds up okra

indicators.note: grinding something up breaks it into pieces and mixes them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also helps signal the mix

explanation.surface: A cook carefully mashes a green vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'grinds up' uses one of its own words as fodder too: SAFELY plus GRINDS rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The slender green pods of okra are commonly called by this name, after their finger-like shape.

clue.text: Developing new ace perfume

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an ace in cards is the A
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A brand-new, first-rate fragrance is being launched.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into existence and starting to grow is at an early, emerging stage.

clue.text: Head of agriculture denies altering strongly flavoured plant

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of agriculture

indicators.note: altering means changing the order of the letters in the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farming chief refuses to change his position on a pungent crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise herb, with a liquorice taste, used in cooking and drinks.

clue.text: Skilled fellow left out of myth

indicators.note: left out of tells us one piece is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: a fable is a myth or legend
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A talented man is missing from an old legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the competence or talent to do something well means being capable.

clue.text: EU actions involved firm

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Brussels' measures involved a company in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a business noun next to EU actions, but it is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding on stubbornly and refusing to give up means being steadfast and determined.

clue.text: Shabby gallery embarrassed to include exhibit finally

indicators.note: to include means to hold something within

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of exhibit
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A run-down gallery is ashamed to hang one more exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra letter sits inside the gallery's name, not inside the colour of embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes worn into ragged, torn pieces look worn-out and in poor condition.

clue.text: Church musician giving up time for European run

indicators.note: giving up one thing for another means exchanging them

parts.note: the person who plays the instrument in church
T is the abbreviation for time
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A church musician quits time-keeping for a run across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of ORGANIST is swapped for E.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an event or business is to manage and arrange it, setting it up in an orderly way.

clue.text: Select a bleach partly suitable for office

indicators.note: partly means only part of the words that precede it is used

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, dropping the S and the ACH

explanation.surface: An instruction to choose a cleaning product that is fit for the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' suggests a workplace where bleach is used, but here it means a public post won at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who could win a vote is fit to be chosen for public position.

clue.text: Rush sculpture by the Parisian

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A hurried glimpse of a statue by a French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy, energetic activity, moving about hurriedly, is a flurry of haste.

clue.text: Blast barrier before end of construction

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of construction

explanation.surface: Engineers set off explosives at a dam before building is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an explosion, but it is the exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are mild curses or exclamations of irritation, used interchangeably.

clue.text: Work with iron causing distress

definitions.note: a participle phrase, while the answer is a plain verb

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Doing the ironing is a stressful chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh heavily on someone or burden them harshly brings them suffering and anxiety.

clue.text: Cut brace loudly

indicators.note: loudly says the word must be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: Someone noisily snips through a support.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim away the outer skin or edge with a knife is to shave off a thin layer.

clue.text: Fall outing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stumble over something
second meaning: a short journey or excursion

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stumbling over an obstacle and a short excursion or journey somewhere.

clue.text: Motor held by men I brutalised on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means reading the letters in the opposite direction
held by means the letters are contained within the following words

parts.note: the letters running from the E of men to the T of brutalised

explanation.surface: Thugs on the return journey beat up an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary engine driven by flowing water, steam or gas, a kind of power unit.

clue.text: Bizarre quarrels about dropping first of questions

indicators.note: about here means turned around and moved about, so the order changes
dropping means letting a letter fall away

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of questions

explanation.surface: Strange arguments break out that avoid the first question.
explanation.walkthrough: Q comes off QUARRELS, leaving UARRELS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamlike and strangely irrational, like the art movement, means weird or odd.

clue.text: Speak fast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put thoughts into words
second meaning: rapid, as in a nonstop train or delivery

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to convey in words and an adjective for high-speed services such as trains.
